The statement recognizes a severe negative shock to demand and supply from COVID-19, but pairs it with an aggressively expansionary stance—cutting the policy rate to the effective lower bound, launching large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanding repo operations, easing discount window terms, and activating dollar swap lines. This response is consistent with the credit channel and financial accelerator literature, which shows that easing financial conditions reduces external finance premia and helps stabilize investment and employment (e.g., Oliner and Rudebusch; Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist). With inflation running below target and market-based inflation compensation falling while survey expectations remain relatively anchored, the Committee’s forward guidance and balance-sheet policies align with inflation forecast targeting principles (Svensson) and are appropriate in a potential liquidity-trap environment where QE and liquidity provision can support aggregate demand and credit intermediation. Netting the near-term economic downside against these powerful stabilization tools implies a moderately negative, but tempered, assessment.
